## Body

#301 and #302 (daemon.log rotation, F251) went through three rounds of the same lesson: a dev/ino check on the path followed by an open by name is a TOCTOU, and each reopen needs its own treatment.

What the hardened shape looks like (crates/cli/src/daemon_log.rs at 6fe4ee2):
- Staging files: remove the leftover, then create_new (O_EXCL) with O_APPEND at 0600, and only under the flock. O_EXCL refuses a symlink re-planted between the remove and the open, so the rotation fails closed. A test that only pre-plants links cannot catch a mutant that drops O_EXCL (ML3); that is a test gap, not an exposure.
- Lock file: create plus O_NOFOLLOW at 0600; never truncate, write or remove it. A symlink, existing or dangling, gives ELOOP and is untouched.
- Join (an open by name after a check): O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK, then fstat is_file. A blocking O_WRONLY open of a FIFO waits for a reader and stalls the log thread while it holds the mutex and the flock.
- Side records (daemon.log.trimmed): read with O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK, capped. A symlink gives ELOOP, a FIFO reads empty, a directory gives EISDIR, and all of them must answer "not recorded" (less adoption).
- Destructive trim: copy the tail, then unlink the name. Never truncate in place, so hard links survive.

Still open after #302 (S302-N1, low): keep_tail reopens its source by name without O_NONBLOCK, fstat or dev/ino == mine. Passing the already-proven fd down is the clean fix.

Severity rule I applied: the default ~/.pij-rs is user-owned 0755, so a planted link needs the same UID, which C33 trusts. That makes these notes, not blocks, unless the state dir can be other-UID writable (--state-dir / PIJ_RS_STATE_DIR). Keep a demonstrated containment break (my round-1 repro truncated an outside file) distinct from whether it is exploitable across UIDs.

Method that worked fast: copy the verbatim Rotation code into a standalone rustc repro in /tmp (no cargo, nice 19), and probe open-flag semantics with python os.open on a symlink, a dangling link, a FIFO and a directory. Both are cheap receipts, with no build and no daemon.

Process: `pij output verdict --answers <req>` already marks the request answered, so a following pij_send reply warns "already answered", which is harmless. To cite a ruling after publishing, re-publish at the same head; it writes a -2 file.
